title: rorca-workspace-billing
_philosophy: Rorca is local-first — no auth wall, no login required, no cloud dependency for basic usage. Free tier = 1 workspace, unlimited specs + runs. Upgrade = more workspaces. The gate is the local SQLite DB (workspace count), NOT user identity. License keys are signed JWTs stored in ~/.rorca/license.json, verified offline via bundled public key. Stripe checkout happens on rorca.app, redirects back to localhost:3030 with the license key. No phone-home required for license verification — the JWT signature is self-contained. This matches the 'local-first, no auth wall' philosophy while enabling monetization.

userStories.title: Change Default Seeded User Plan to 'free'
userStories.description: The default admin user (admin@rorca.local) is currently seeded with plan='pro' in db/index.ts. This must be 'free' so new installs start on the free tier (1 workspace). New database creation (first rorca start) seeds admin@rorca.local with plan='free'

userStories.title: License Key Infrastructure — Generate, Store, Verify Offline
userStories.description: Implement the license key system. License keys are RS256-signed JWTs containing tier + expiry. The public key is bundled in the npm package for offline verification. The private key lives only on the cloud/Stripe side (rorca.app). License keys are stored in ~/.rorca/license.json and read on backend startup.
acceptanceCriteria: New file: backend/src/lib/license.ts — exports getLicenseTier(), verifyLicenseKey(), activateLicense()
License key format: RS256-signed JWT with payload { tier: 'solo'|'pro'|'team', email: string, issuedAt: number, expiresAt: number, machineId?: string }
Public key bundled as a constant string in license.ts (RS256 public key, ~450 bytes) — used for OFFLINE verification, no network call needed
Private key is NOT in the codebase — it lives only on the cloud licensing server (rorca.app)
getLicenseTier() reads ~/.rorca/license.json → verifies JWT signature with bundled public key → returns tier string or 'free' if missing/invalid/expired
License file path resolved from RORCA_HOME env var (set by bin/rorca.ts to ~/.rorca/) with fallback to path.join(os.homedir(), '.rorca', 'license.json')
license.json format: { key: '<jwt-string>', activatedAt: '<ISO-8601>', email: '<user-email>' }
If license.json doesn't exist: getLicenseTier() returns 'free' (no error, no log — normal state for free tier)
If license.json exists but JWT signature is invalid: log warning '[license] Invalid license key — reverting to free tier', return 'free'
If license.json exists but JWT is expired: log info '[license] License expired on {date} — reverting to free tier', return 'free'
getLicenseTier() caches the result in a module-level variable — re-reads the file only on explicit invalidation (after activation) or every 60 minutes
activateLicense(keyString) writes license.json and invalidates the cache, returns the decoded tier
TypeScript types exported: LicensePayload, LicenseTier = 'free' | 'solo' | 'pro' | 'team'

userStories.title: Wire License Tier into requirePlan Middleware
userStories.description: The existing requirePlan middleware reads the user's plan from the DB (users.plan column). For local-first mode (no auth), it should also check the license key tier and use the HIGHER of the two. This way, a license key upgrade takes effect without needing to modify the DB.
acceptanceCriteria: In backend/src/lib/require-plan.ts, import getLicenseTier() from license.ts
When resolving the effective plan: effectivePlan = max(user.plan, getLicenseTier()) where tier ordering is free < solo < pro < team
Add a TIER_ORDER constant: { free: 0, solo: 1, pro: 2, team: 3 } for comparison
The higher tier wins — if user.plan='free' and license='pro', effective plan is 'pro'
If both are 'free', workspace limit is 1 (from plan_quotas table, already seeded)
The 402 response body includes the effective plan and the license tier for debugging: { currentPlan: effectivePlan, licenseTier: licenseTier, dbPlan: user.plan }
No change to the quota calculation logic — it still reads from plan_quotas table using the effective plan
requirePlan continues to work for all features (workspaces, specs_per_month, team_members, etc.), not just workspaces
getLicenseTier() is called once per request (cached in module variable, negligible cost)

userStories.title: License Activation Endpoint — POST /api/billing/activate
userStories.description: Add an endpoint that receives a license key JWT (from Stripe redirect or manual paste), verifies it, stores it in ~/.rorca/license.json, and returns the activated tier. This is the callback target for the Stripe checkout flow.
acceptanceCriteria: New route: POST /api/billing/activate — accepts { key: string } in request body
No auth required on this endpoint — it's part of the no-auth-wall local-first flow
Validates the JWT signature using the bundled public key (same as getLicenseTier())
If signature is invalid: returns 400 { error: 'Invalid license key', code: 'INVALID_LICENSE' }
If JWT is expired: returns 400 { error: 'License key has expired', code: 'LICENSE_EXPIRED', expiresAt: '<date>' }
If valid: calls activateLicense(key) from license.ts → writes ~/.rorca/license.json
Also updates the local user's plan in the DB: UPDATE users SET plan = ? WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM users LIMIT 1)
Updating the DB ensures consistency — both license.json AND users.plan reflect the tier
Returns 200 { tier: 'pro', email: 'user@example.com', expiresAt: '<ISO-8601>', message: 'License activated successfully' }
Emits a WAL event: event_type='license_activated', payload includes { tier, email, expiresAt }
Backend log: '[billing] License activated: {tier} tier, expires {date}'
GET /api/billing/activate?key=<jwt> also works (for Stripe redirect URL callback — GET with query param for browser redirect compatibility)
GET variant redirects to the frontend settings page after activation: 302 redirect to /?activated={tier}
Frontend detects ?activated= query param and shows a success toast: 'Upgraded to {tier} — you can now add more workspaces'

userStories.title: Stripe Checkout Flow — Local-First with rorca.app Redirect
userStories.description: Configure the Stripe checkout session to work with local-first billing. The checkout happens on Stripe's hosted page, but the success redirect points back to localhost:3030 with the license key. Since Stripe can't generate the license key directly, a lightweight cloud function on rorca.app acts as the intermediary: Stripe webhook → cloud function generates signed JWT → redirects to localhost:3030/api/billing/activate.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/billing/checkout updated: success_url set to RORCA_CLOUD_URL/api/license/fulfill?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}&port={localPort}
RORCA_CLOUD_URL env var (default: 'https://rorca.app') — the cloud endpoint that signs license keys
cancel_url set to http://localhost:{port}/settings/billing (returns to local settings page)
Stripe checkout metadata includes: { localPort: PORT, machineId: os.hostname() } so the cloud fulfillment endpoint knows where to redirect

The cloud fulfillment endpoint (NOT in this codebase — documented as external dependency) does: verify Stripe session → extract plan → sign JWT with private key → redirect to http://localhost:{port}/api/billing/activate?key={jwt}

Documentation added as a comment block in billing.ts explaining the full flow: User clicks Upgrade → POST /api/billing/checkout → Stripe hosted page → payment → Stripe redirects to rorca.app/api/license/fulfill → cloud signs JWT → redirects to localhost:3030/api/billing/activate?key=jwt → license.json written → user sees success
If STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not configured: POST /api/billing/checkout returns 503 { error: 'Billing not configured', suggestion: 'Visit rorca.app/pricing to upgrade' }
Fallback: if cloud fulfillment fails (user closes browser, network issue), Settings > Billing shows 'Enter license key manually' input field
The manual key entry field calls POST /api/billing/activate with the pasted JWT

userStories.title: Frontend 402 Interceptor — Catch Plan Limit Errors Globally
userStories.description: Add a global fetch interceptor that catches 402 responses and triggers the PaywallModal. This ensures ANY plan-gated feature (workspaces, specs, marketplace) shows the upgrade prompt automatically without each component handling it individually.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/lib/apiFetch.ts, add 402 response handling to the global fetch wrapper
When a 402 response is received: parse the JSON body (expects { error, feature, currentPlan, requiredPlan, currentUsage, quotaLimit })
Emit a custom event: window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('rorca:paywall', { detail: parsedBody }))
New context: src/contexts/PaywallContext.tsx — provides PaywallProvider wrapping the app in App.tsx
PaywallProvider listens for 'rorca:paywall' events and renders PaywallModal with the event detail as props

userStories.title: 14-Day Full-Featured Trial on Fresh Install
userStories.description: Every great SaaS tool gives users a trial before asking for payment. Raycast, Linear, Vercel, and Retool all do this. Rorca should start every fresh install with a 14-day full-featured trial — pro tier access with unlimited workspaces, no payment required. Trial state is tracked in `~/.rorca/license.json` as `{ type: 'trial', installedAt: '<ISO>', expiresAt: '<ISO +14d>', tier: 'pro' }`. The trial starts automatically on first `rorca start` with no user action required. When the trial expires, the user is downgraded to free tier (1 workspace) with an upgrade CTA. The trial banner in Settings > Billing is prominent but not intrusive — shown as an amber info bar with days remaining and a one-click 'Upgrade Now' button. The BIL-003 requirePlan middleware must treat 'trial' as equivalent to 'pro' for feature gating. Trial users do NOT need a license key or Stripe account.

BIL-003 requirePlan middleware checks: tier='trial' && expiresAt > now → treat as 'pro'
BIL-003 requirePlan: tier='trial' && expiresAt < now → treat as 'free' (1 workspace limit enforced)
BIL-008 License Status Display in Settings Billing tab shows trial state: 'Trial — X days remaining'

When trial is expired: red banner with 'Your trial has ended. Upgrade to continue.' + Upgrade Now button
Upgrade Now button links to Stripe checkout (BIL-005)
Trial tier ('pro') shows on the billing status card: 'Trial Pro Plan — expires Mar 26, 2026'

userStories.title: Automatic License Key Delivery and One-Click Web Activation
userStories.description: The current flow requires users to copy-paste a license key manually after Stripe checkout. SOTA billing UX (Paddle, LemonSqueezy, Gumroad) auto-delivers the license immediately after payment. Two delivery paths: (1) Email delivery — Stripe `checkout.session.completed` webhook triggers license generation and sends an email with the license key + one-click activation link. (2) One-click activation URL — the activation link uses a custom URL scheme `rorca://activate?key=<license>` that the CLI intercepts. On macOS/Linux, this requires registering the `rorca://` protocol handler during install. Fallback: a web activation page at `https://get.rorca.app/activate?key=<license>` that shows the CLI command to paste. The Stripe webhook signing secret must be validated (HMAC-SHA256) before processing — raw webhook without signature check is a security vulnerability.
acceptanceCriteria: Stripe webhook handler in backend/src/routes/billing.ts validates webhook signature: stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(rawBody, sig, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) — rejects if invalid
On checkout.session.completed: generate RS256 license key (BIL-002), send email to customer_email with license key + activation link
Email template: plain text + HTML, subject 'Your Rorca license key', body includes the key in a monospace code block + one-click activation link
Activation link format: https://get.rorca.app/activate?key={base64url-encoded-key}&email={email}
GET /api/billing/activate-redirect?key={key} redirects to rorca://activate?key={key} (triggers CLI handler) or shows fallback page
rorca://activate custom URL scheme registered in install.sh: `open -a 'Rorca' rorca://activate` on macOS (requires rorca binary registered as URL handler)
CLI handles rorca://activate?key=... argument: extracts key, calls POST /api/billing/activate, shows 'License activated! You are now on the Pro plan.' success message
Fallback page at /activate (if URL scheme fails or browser blocks it): shows `rorca license activate <key>` command in a copyable code block
Email delivery uses nodemailer with SMTP credentials from env vars: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS — or falls back to console.log in development
POST /api/billing/activate endpoint (BIL-004) returns { activated: true, tier, expiresAt } — response includes tier for immediate UI update
License keys generated on webhook are persisted to a licenses table (id, email, key_hash, tier, created_at) — not just sent and forgotten
Webhook idempotency: duplicate checkout.session.completed events (Stripe retries) do not generate duplicate licenses — check licenses table for existing entry by session_id
